note: character_id is the STORY identity. It never changes, and narrative/dialogue/
quest code must reference ONLY character_id -- never placeholder_model.
placeholder_model is the rehearsal costume. It is expected to be replaced, and
replacing it must be a one-line edit in this file with no other change anywhere.
These low-poly actors are REHEARSAL ACTORS: they may be ugly, but they must not
change a character's design. If a model is wrong for a role, change the model.

female_medium.why_this_field: A model swap is only safe if the skeleton behaves the same. rig_repairs records what had to be corrected on import; a new model that needs DIFFERENT repairs is a different profile, not a drop-in.

male_medium.why_this_field: Same clip, same retarget, no repair -- the two packs are NOT the same rig. See docs/characters/DEMO_CAST.md section 4.

base_motions._comment: The shared vocabulary from the brief section 7. 'clips' lists library clips that already satisfy it; status is covered/partial/missing so the remaining authoring work is a list, not a feeling.

Look.plan: head-only additive on Idle; no library clip. Cheapest useful authoring target.

Point.plan: upper-body additive; needed by Taim (indicate) and Mira (point_finding).

Turn.plan: needed the moment an NPC walks_to a marker. Author as a pose variant of Walk.

Start.plan: Walk in-blend; can be a 0.2s additive lead-in.

Carry.plan: Interact is a reach, not a carry. Town life needs a real carry (crate/sack).

Stand.plan: Sitting_Exit ends standing but is keyed to a seat height.

animation_profiles._comment: The CHARACTER LAYER from the brief section 6: one shared base motion, per-character pose/timing variant. Four fully separate walk cycles were explicitly NOT wanted.

walk.note: light and steady; she is used to moving

talk.note: he does not stop working to talk; gesture is the work

walk.note: slightly quicker; thinking ahead of her feet

talk.note: fast small gestures, not stage waving

walk.note: injured; replaces the base walk outright

characters.cast_reason: Utility wear, boots, ponytail, no ornament. She works on a river, not in a hall.

DEVIATES FROM THE BRIEF. The brief proposed worker_m; its hi-vis safety vest and hard hat read 'municipal works crew', a hard modern signifier in a misty fantasy village. farmer_m (straw hat, cloth shirt, overalls) reads 'person who works with their hands outdoors', which is the role. See the A/B sheet.
Asymmetric modern functional wear. A pointed hat would declare 'traditional witch' before she says a word, which is the one thing the role must not be.

GENUINE TOSS-UP, user's call. suit_w reads 'administrator' more sharply but imports a modern office signifier; formal_w is period-neutral and reads 'townsfolk in formal dress'. Default kept as the brief's pick. One-line change in this file if you disagree.
characters.id_note: The narrative spells this character 'Vell' (docs/narrative/CHARACTERS.md section 6). The brief wrote 'Veil'. The manifest follows the narrative; 'veil' is NOT an accepted alias.

characters.cast_reason: Must not read as a hero. He is the ordinary person the player's first fight happened to.
characters.soft_note: casual2_m (plain tee, jeans) reads slightly older and more work-worn; casual_m's shorts read younger. Either is defensible.

characters.cast_reason: ADDED BY ME, not in the brief's map, but he has a DAILY PRESENCE entry and is the player's first roof and first paying work. The tradesman read is the closest this pack has to a smith.
ADDED BY ME. He is the only NPC who walks up to the player, and he is sixteen -- the plainest male model is the correct one.
characters.narrative_note: CHARACTERS.md is internally inconsistent: section 1 titles him 'Arn', the section 14 table says 'Ano'. Flagged for narrative, not resolved here; the manifest uses 'arn'.

characters.cast_reason: ADDED BY ME. He is the registration gate the player fails at. Drawn from the guard pool on purpose: his function is procedural, not heroic.
characters.world_note: The model's real-world 'SWAT' meaning must never reach the world bible. It is a GUARD ACTOR.

characters.cast_reason: The brief's 'Guild Lead'. His whole manner is paperwork and exhaustion, not authority in armour.

Registered and deliberately NOT animated. In Act I this character exists only as rumour -- nobody has seen them. king_m was rejected outright: its crown is a hard 'he is a king' signifier and would leak a design decision the narrative has not made.
characters.world_law: No name, no face, no background in Act I.

town_crowd.naming: town_citizen_01 .. town_citizen_NN -- generic instances, NO stable story id, ever
town_crowd.actions: town_carry_crate, town_sweep, town_sit, town_talk, town_walk, town_inspect_stall, town_move_sack
town_crowd.discipline: Do NOT all stand on marks rocking left-right. A town reads as inhabited when people are doing something to something.

guard.world_note: GUARD ACTORS. No real-world unit meaning is imported.
guard.why_not_swat_m: swat_m IS Brann (the ferry warden). Putting it in the background guard pool too would let a villager read as a named character.

hostile_humanoid_test.discipline: Test-only. The Act I first enemy is 遗迹哨兵, which is NOT human. Having humanoid actors must not change that.

not_cast_as_villagers.why: Each carries a hard out-of-genre signifier (crown, spacesuit, pointed witch hat, mohawk). Putting one in a Mistvale crowd would spend a first impression the narrative has not made yet.

deliberately_uncast.why: Nothing in this pack reads as non-human. Do NOT turn her into a human to make a model fit -- that is changing character design to suit a placeholder.
First impression is a narrative asset. Spending it on a generic casual model is worse than not appearing.
Not needed on screen yet; no binding until the narrative asks for her.
